headline: Mistakes to Avoid in a Federal Criminal Investigation

publisher.name: Law Office of Angelo J. Reyes, APC

articleBody: Navigating a federal criminal investigation is a high-stakes situation, and a few common missteps can seriously jeopardize your outcome. Let's look at some big ones to steer clear of. First off, don't talk to federal agents without your lawyer present. They're highly trained and their job is to gather information that can be used against you, even if they seem friendly. Politely state you want your attorney before answering any questions. Secondly, never provide false information or destroy documents. Doing so can lead to new charges like perjury or obstruction of justice, making your legal situation far worse than it already is. Always be truthful with your attorney, but remember your right to remain silent with investigators. Another common error is thinking you can handle it yourself. Federal cases involve complex laws and procedures that differ significantly from state cases. Trying to represent yourself or relying on general legal advice is a huge risk. You need someone who knows the federal system inside and out. Lastly, don't delay in seeking legal counsel. The earlier an experienced federal criminal defense attorney gets involved, the more they can do to protect your rights, investigate the facts, and build a strong defense. Waiting only gives the prosecution more time to build their case against you.
